papers.title: On-Policy or Off-Policy Learning? A Systematic Study of Distillation Dynamics

summary.tldr: A controlled study on Llama3 and Qwen2.5 shows rollout policy is less critical than token-level KL direction for task performance, while learning rate drives forgetting and update sparsity.
key_points: Forward KL is highly robust to rollout policy shifts, maintaining stable performance across the student-teacher policy spectrum.
Reverse KL is significantly more sensitive to the rollout policy and performs better when using student-generated rollouts.
Learning rate, rather than on-policy data, primarily governs catastrophic forgetting and the sparsity of parameter updates.
On-policy data enhances generalization on harder Countdown arithmetic variants for both KL directions, but the advantage wanes after subsequent RLVR.
summary.why_it_matters: The findings challenge the assumption that on-policy rollouts are inherently superior, helping practitioners optimize distillation pipelines by prioritizing KL direction and learning rates over complex policy data generation.

papers.title: Transformers Stop Thinking Too Early, and a Tiny LoRA Fixes It

summary.tldr: A task-trained rank-8 LoRA applied to a single early layer enables frozen pretrained transformers to process significantly longer in-context reference chains by initiating a hidden state relay across middle layers.
key_points: Pretrained transformers default to following only 1.4-3.6 lines of context references, and adding pretrained loops yields minimal gain.
Applying a rank-8 LoRA to one early layer improves Qwen3-8B's exact accuracy on 24-line chains from 15.5% to 99%, with longer training extending performance to 50 lines.
Ouro-1.4B with the LoRA edit processes 60 lines after four loops and at least 160 lines after eight loops.
The edit triggers a relay where middle layers pass chain identity and frozen heads attend progressively further up the chain; removing parent-line attention breaks the mechanism.
A frozen-model measurement successfully predicts the last effective intervention layer within tolerance across three of four held-out models.
summary.why_it_matters: A minimal, single-layer parameter edit unlocks deep contextual reasoning capabilities that remain latent and underutilized in default pretrained transformers.

papers.title: Video Generation Models: A Survey of Post-Training and Alignment

summary.tldr: This survey provides the first comprehensive review of post-training and alignment techniques in video generation models, categorizing them into a taxonomy of implicit and explicit alignment across four methodological paradigms.
key_points: Identifies video alignment challenges including temporal error accumulation, motion-appearance coupling, multi-objective trade-offs, and sparse temporal supervision.
Establishes a taxonomy categorizing approaches into supervised fine-tuning, self-training/distillation, preference/reward-based methods, and inference-time methods.
Distinguishes alignment techniques by implicit versus explicit enforcement of alignment signals across training and deployment phases.
Reviews evaluation frameworks, datasets, benchmarks, and open issues such as scalable reward design, long-horizon temporal consistency, and safety constraints.
summary.why_it_matters: It offers a structured framework to adapt pretrained video models for improved controllability, temporal consistency, and safety without requiring full retraining from scratch.

papers.title: Decoding Looped Transformers Better for (Almost) Free

summary.tldr: LoopCD is a training-free contrastive decoding framework for looped Transformers that uses intermediate recurrent states as guidance to improve inference quality while reducing compute.
key_points: Leverages inherent weak-and-strong prediction pairs from early and late recurrent passes without requiring auxiliary models or external training.
Offers two implementation variants: LoopCD-Logits (contrasts predictions in logit space with one extra output pass) and LoopCD-Hidden (contrasts in hidden-state space with zero output overhead).
LoopCD-Logits increases Ouro-2.6B-Thinking's AIME 2024 pass@1 from 61.88% to 73.33%, while LoopCD-Hidden improves Huginn's HumanEval pass@1 from 22.56% to 31.71%.
Allows halving the number of recurrent loops to match or exceed full-depth unguided baselines, reducing forward FLOPs by 22.5% to 48.2%.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves LLM reasoning performance and significantly cuts inference FLOPs for parameter-efficient looped architectures without requiring additional model training.

papers.title: Persona Dosing: Calibrated Activation Steering for Graded Trait Control

summary.tldr: PersonaDose introduces calibrated activation steering to control language model persona traits by specializing a shared FLAS controller and calibrating flow time against measured trait intensity.
key_points: PersonaDose specializes a description-conditioned FLAS controller on persona responses without needing training responses paired with target intensities.
Outperforms contrastive activation addition at the Persona Vectors 75 coherence floor by 33.2 points on Llama-3.1-8B, 18.3 points on Qwen3-8B, and 17.8 points on Gemma-3-4B.
Achieves mean targeting errors between 4.7 and 6.2 points across 14 to 22 calibration-reachable targets (out of 28 total per model) over seven trained traits.
Demonstrates that the behavioral range learned by an activation controller is distinct from the accuracy of specific intensity requests within that range.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables precise, graded behavioral control over language model traits using calibrated intensity requests rather than uncalibrated steering coefficients.

papers.title: Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes

summary.tldr: Where-OPD is an on-policy self-distillation method for MLLMs where a teacher model receives privileged textual spatial guidance from procedurally generated synthetic scenes, enhancing student perception without external models or human annotations.
key_points: Uses synthetic, procedurally generated scenes with automatically extracted object identities and spatial coordinates as privileged textual guidance for the teacher model.
The teacher integrates evidence from multiple image regions using spatial guidance, while the student is trained on-policy using only the raw image and query.
Eliminates reliance on visual zooming, human-annotated visual grounding data, or larger external teacher models.
Achieves a 3.23-point average performance gain across real-world perception benchmarks including CVBench, V*, ZoomBench, BLINK, HR-Bench, and MME-RealWorld.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that synthetic, spatially guided self-distillation transfers effectively to real-world visual perception and reasoning tasks without requiring costly human annotations.

papers.title: Better Supervision Is Nearby: Neighborhood On-Policy Self-Distillation

summary.tldr: Neighborhood On-Policy Self-Distillation (N-OPSD) improves mathematical reasoning models by using local parameter perturbations to create a pool of frozen expert teachers that supervise student-sampled prefixes.
key_points: Offline pool selection uses greedy optimization to pick frozen experts based on filtered reference-token gains beyond the pool's current best at each position.
Online routing separates anchor selection via MaxPeak from support-level selection using quantile choice among experts matching the anchor token.
Students learn the selected expert's full next-token distribution using OPSD's clipped forward-KL objective, retaining standard single-model inference.
N-OPSD improves Average@12 accuracy over standard OPSD across AIME 2024, AIME 2025, and HMMT Feb 2025 by 2.75, 1.67, and 1.94 points on Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B models, respectively.
summary.why_it_matters: N-OPSD extracts stronger, position-specific supervision from parameter perturbations during training without adding memory or compute overhead at inference time.

papers.title: Ego2Act: Evaluating Goal-Directed Manipulation in Egocentric Video Generation

summary.tldr: Ego2Act is a new benchmark featuring 2,640 egocentric videos across 110 real-world tasks to evaluate goal-directed, multi-step physical manipulation in video generation models.
key_points: Introduces Ego2Act, containing 2,640 videos from 110 tasks designed to test multi-step physical reasoning from an initial image and high-level goal.
Features Ego2ActJudge, a reference-free evaluation pipeline that assesses task completion and physical plausibility with stronger human alignment than existing baselines.
Reveals that current models frequently skip or partially execute intermediate steps, causing missing dependent states in later steps.
Demonstrates consistent model failures in fine-grained physical dynamics, complex hand-object manipulation, and persistent world modeling.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a rigorous framework to benchmark whether video generation models can function as physically plausible world simulators for embodied planning and AI robotics.

papers.title: VTR-Bench: A Systematic Benchmark for Evaluating Visual Text Rendering in Video Generation

summary.tldr: VTR-Bench evaluates visual text rendering in video generation models across 300 prompts and five scenarios, introducing an automated evaluation pipeline and a Keyframe-Guided Agentic Framework to iteratively refine generated output.
key_points: VTR-Bench contains 300 prompts covering five application scenarios, including advertisements and scientific videos.
The automated evaluation pipeline assesses text fidelity using carrier-specific transcription and evaluates scene and motion requirements via a prompt-specific chain of query.
A Keyframe-Guided Agentic Framework uses a Director agent to coordinate image/video generation with visual evaluation for iterative refinement based on visual feedback.
Evaluation of 11 state-of-the-art video generation models revealed widespread text rendering failures, with the top-performing model achieving an overall word error rate (WER) of 0.250.
summary.why_it_matters: It exposes a critical failure mode in current video generation models and provides a standardized benchmark and agentic workflow to improve in-scene text accuracy.

papers.title: AgSpec: Pushing the Limits of Retrieval-Based Speculative Decoding in Coding Agent Pipelines

summary.tldr: AgSpec improves retrieval-based speculative decoding in coding agents by retrieving from session, workspace, and global corpora while dynamically managing draft lengths through offline profiling and online feedback.
key_points: Retrieves from session trajectories, workspace files, and global corpora, indexing open files in the agent's specific emission format.
Applies an offline-profiled draft length cap alongside online adaptive adjustment based on verification feedback.
Achieves generation throughput gains over autoregressive decoding of up to 4.37x at batch size 1 and 4.76x at batch size 16.
Outperforms five retrieval-based drafting baselines and EAGLE-3 across repository-level multi-agent coding benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly accelerates inference speeds for LLM-based coding agents without requiring extra neural draft models, reducing pipeline latency and cost.

papers.title: SemanTok: Predictable Semantic Tokens for Efficient Autoregressive Video Generation

summary.tldr: SemanTok is a flexible video tokenizer that feeds frozen DINO features into its encoder and uses lightweight heads to reconstruct semantic features directly from retained token prefixes.
key_points: Feeds frozen DINO features into the encoder and adds lightweight heads that reconstruct them solely from retained token prefixes.
Provides higher semantic alignment to the decoder across all noise levels, including pure noise, and maintains alignment on out-of-distribution classes.
Enables a 201M parameter SemanTok autoregressive model to match or outperform a VideoFlexTok model 3.4 times its size.
Defers pixel details to later tokens, allowing shorter token prefixes to lower prediction costs while improving generation fidelity.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves autoregressive video generation efficiency and fidelity by enabling smaller models to achieve performance superior to significantly larger baselines using shorter token prefixes.

papers.title: Removing the NEEDLE in the Haystack: Backdoor Removal in LLMs via Weight Orthogonalisation

summary.tldr: NEEDLE is a training-free backdoor removal method for LLMs that uses activation vectors and sequential weight orthogonalisation to eliminate triggers without degrading safety or general capabilities.
key_points: Estimates a backdoor direction and refusal subspace using activation vectors after a trigger is identified.
Applies sequential weight orthogonalisation to suppress the backdoor while preserving refusal-related representations.
Operates without requiring a clean reference model or access to the original poisoned training dataset.
Achieves 0% Attack Success Rate (ASR) on code injection attacks and records the lowest mean ASR and KL divergence among evaluated defenses.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables post-hoc mitigation of LLM backdoor attacks without requiring retraining, clean baseline models, or sacrificing general model safety and utility.

papers.title: DataMagic: Authoring Data Videos through Declarative Multi-Agent Orchestration

summary.tldr: DataMagic generates data videos from raw tabular data using a declarative specification (DVSpec) and a multi-agent orchestration framework that optimizes narrative coherence.
key_points: DVSpec unifies charts, narration, and animations using data-bound references and declarative synchronization to ensure data accuracy and audio-visual alignment.
Employs a 'Generate-then-Orchestrate' multi-agent strategy that creates candidate scenes in parallel and refines global narrative coherence.
Provides a shared state across DVSpec supporting full automation alongside fine-grained human editing across three interaction modes.
Outperforms baseline LLMs on 109 samples by increasing quality scores from 2.13/5 to 3.89/5 and boosting execution success rates to over 95%.
Reduces task creation time by 79.7% and lowers perceived cognitive load compared to conversational LLM workflows.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables automated, data-accurate video generation from raw tabular inputs while significantly reducing manual editing time and cognitive effort.

papers.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research

summary.tldr: ScholarCatalyst is a benchmark based on annotations from 184 lead authors evaluating model ability to retrieve literature that inspired their recent computer science papers.
key_points: Dataset contains annotations from 184 lead authors across 207 computer science papers, paired with detailed rationales for past literature that advanced their work.
The retrieval task challenges models to find catalytic papers from historical literature available only at the project's inception given an initial research question.
Standard agentic search achieves 0.42 Recall@20, performing worse than simple embedding retrieval at 0.48 Recall@20 despite using the same retriever.
An agent utilizing Claude Fable 5.1 achieves a top Recall@20 of 0.51, demonstrating current AI limitations in replicating expert scientific intuition.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a benchmark proving that current AI agents and search techniques lack the expert intuition required to navigate broad literature archives and locate foundational ideas for new research.

papers.title: LOCI: Spatial Linear Memory for Streaming World Models

summary.tldr: LOCI is a hybrid spatial-memory world model architecture that combines a visual key-value cache with a recurrent linear-attention memory conditioned on projective camera geometry for streaming video synthesis.
key_points: LOCI uses full key-value attention caches in half of its transformer blocks and chunk-restricted attention paired with geometry-conditioned recurrent memory in the other half.
Recurrent memory reads and writes use projective camera geometry to incorporate viewpoint into memory addressing and stored content.
Recurrent readouts feed accumulated scene context into subsequent cache-backed transformer blocks.
LOCI reduces peak memory usage by ~30% compared to full-softmax attention at equal context length and enables long-video streaming at constant memory with a bounded observation bank.
Evaluations on the MIND memory benchmark and held-out trajectories show improved reproduction of revisited visual content over full-softmax baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: LOCI allows streaming video world models to maintain spatial memory consistency when revisiting locations while operating within a fixed GPU memory budget.

papers.title: Asynchronous LLM Post-Training: Group-Mass Capping and Convergence Analysis

summary.tldr: Group Mass Capping GRPO (GMC-GRPO) mitigates stale-rollout bias in asynchronous LLM post-training, reducing the fourth-order delay term's threshold dependence from O(ε⁻⁴) to O(ε⁻²).
key_points: Derived a GRPO convergence bound that isolates the tradeoff between the second moment of trajectory-level importance-weighted estimators and bias from clipping or rescaling.
GMC-GRPO minimizes a ratio-based bias bound among weighted estimators with identical second-moment guarantees, reducing delay dependence as G⁻²ᐟ⁵ under local policy overlap.
Group rescaling bias vanishes as group size G→∞ for fixed policies, whereas trajectory-wise clipping bias persists.
Empirical validation on Qwen3 models and reasoning benchmarks demonstrates improved robustness and stability under large rollout delays compared to TIC-GRPO and baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: GMC-GRPO enables stable, efficient asynchronous RL post-training for LLMs under heavy rollout delays without persistent clipping bias.

papers.title: Universal Byte-Level Encoding: UTF-8/UTF-16 Routing to Reduce Cross-Script Token-Budget Disparities

summary.tldr: Universal Byte-Level Encoding (UBE) routes 1-2-byte UTF-8 characters through UTF-8 and 3-4-byte characters through UTF-16 before BPE to reduce token-budget disparities across scripts without compromising English efficiency or decoding accuracy.
key_points: Addresses the high worst-case pre-merge encoding floor of UTF-8 BBPE for non-English scripts by lowering the floor for 3-byte Basic Multilingual Plane (BMP) characters.
Maintains standard BPE merge rules and exact decoding, successfully passing full Unicode 17 normalization, grapheme-break, and emoji test suites.
Composes with alternative boundary policies and morphology-based representations.
Reduces token counts most for high-premium scripts while slightly lowering English token counts, improving context utilization and prompt processing speeds without sacrificing LM quality.
summary.why_it_matters: UBE reduces cross-lingual token cost inequities and expands usable context window sizes in multilingual LLMs without altering core BPE algorithms or degrading performance in English.

papers.title: Same Reward, Different Skills: When Multimodal RL Learns to Look

summary.tldr: Researchers show that standard RLVR induces visual grounding skills only when tasks enforce visual resolvability, requiring visual evidence for success rather than allowing shortcuts through text or language-only heuristics.
key_points: Blind-trained RL models using test images recover 50% (at 3B) to nearly 80% (at 7B) of real-image benchmark gains, proving standard benchmarks permit language-only shortcuts.
Prolonged training on real images can erode visual grounding even as benchmark scores continue to improve.
Enforcing visual resolvability on counterfactual coordinate scenes using standard GRPO raised 7B model target discovery accuracy from 0.425 to 0.875 on dense, held-out scenes.
Adding a text caption that answered the training question to the images reduced discovery gains by nearly two-thirds under identical reward structures and compute budgets.
Testing with gray canvases dropped discovery to zero, and training on gray canvases yielded no gain when evaluated with real images.
summary.why_it_matters: To build truly grounded multimodal models, benchmark and RL task designs must require visual information to solve the problem rather than relying solely on text-based correctness rewards.

papers.title: GAW-PO: Preference Optimization with Gradient-Aligned Token Weights

summary.tldr: GAW-PO improves Direct Preference Optimization by reweighting rejected tokens based on gradient alignment with preferred updates, preventing useful tokens in rejected responses from being unfairly penalized.
key_points: Identifies a flaw in standard DPO where all tokens in a rejected response, including potentially useful ones, are penalized equally.
Calculates token-level gradient alignment to weaken the negative penalty for rejected tokens that align with preferred behavior.
Outperforms standard DPO by 0.97 points and the best baseline by 0.65 points on average across 11 benchmarks in math, coding, reasoning, and QA.
Demonstrates superior robustness when scaling the regularization parameter β downwards, where standard DPO degrades but GAW-PO improves.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides effective token-level credit assignment in preference tuning, preventing models from degrading when aggressively optimized using lower β values.

papers.title: No Model Required: Text Entropy Rate Filtering Mitigates Iterative Fine-Tuning Collapse

summary.tldr: Researchers developed a non-parametric text entropy rate estimator, Kontoyiannis $h_k$, that mitigates model collapse during iterative fine-tuning on synthetic data without requiring model log-probabilities, external oracles, or human data.
key_points: Uses match-length statistics from raw text to calculate the Kontoyiannis entropy rate $h_k$ without using any model.
Tested in a six-generation QLoRA collapse experiment on Llama-3.1-8B, where logprob-based filtering provided no statistically significant text-diversity benefit ($p > 0.23$).
Filtering with $h_k$ increased unique trigrams by 42% and vocabulary by 30%, while reducing text repetition by 19% (all $p < 0.001$).
Validated $h_k$ as a cross-domain entropy proxy ($ eta = 0.924$, $R^2 = 0.746$) and collapse detector ($ho = +0.454$, $p < 0.0001$) across 1,520 documents.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables model-agnostic, computationally efficient training-data filtering that preserves text diversity and prevents model degradation across successive generations of synthetic fine-tuning.

papers.title: Gacha Decoding: Eliciting Diverse Generations Through Instruction Following

summary.tldr: Gacha Decoding is an inference-time method that replaces token entropy sampling with instruction-following and external random number generation to improve language model output diversity.
key_points: Combines instruction-following capabilities with an external RNG tool to explicitly plan and generate distinct response modes.
Outperforms prior diversity methods by up to 2.4x on the Vendi score at equal output quality.
Achieves equivalent high-quality mode coverage using 11.0x fewer samples compared to existing baseline approaches.
Inverts the traditional trade-off between model capability and diversity, causing generation diversity to scale directly with instruction-following performance.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables developers to extract significantly more diverse, high-quality outputs and discover novel response modes from capable language models while drastically reducing the required sample count.

papers.title: FERPO: Forward Entropy-Regularized Policy Optimization

summary.tldr: Forward Entropy-Regularized Policy Optimization (FERPO) is an on-policy maximum entropy RL algorithm that updates actors using critic values directly, avoiding action-derivative critic gradients.
key_points: Eliminates the need to differentiate the critic with respect to actions by deriving an optimal target action distribution from entropy- and KL-regularized policy improvement.
Fits the actor to the target distribution by minimizing a forward Kullback-Leibler (KL) objective using self-normalized importance sampling (SNIS).
Uses KL regularization to restrict target distribution deviation from the rollout policy, maintaining well-behaved importance weights.
Leverages forward-KL to cover multiple high-value action modes and enhance exploration, contrasting with reverse-KL mode-seeking behavior.
Demonstrates improved sample efficiency on MuJoCo Playground and ManiSkill, with faster actor updates than Relative Entropy Pathwise Policy Optimization (REPPO).
summary.why_it_matters: FERPO avoids unreliable policy updates caused by inaccurate critic action-derivatives while offering faster execution and better multi-modal exploration in continuous control tasks.

papers.title: SoftServe: A Scalable Quasi-Newton Method for Deep Learning

summary.tldr: SoftServe is a scalable quasi-Newton optimization method using variational curvature estimates and coupled Newton-Schulz iterations to handle non-convexity and high parameter counts without line searches.
key_points: Derives positive-definite curvature estimates from the variational objective of Berglund et al. (2025) to handle negative curvature.
Features diagonal and Kronecker-factored variants that maintain positive definiteness by construction.
Uses stable coupled Newton-Schulz iterations instead of matrix decompositions, converting matrix operations into GPU-friendly matrix multiplications.
Outperforms Adam, Muon, and SOAP on ill-conditioned tasks, including recurrent networks, deep autoencoders, physics-informed neural networks, and a 136M-parameter diffusion model.
summary.why_it_matters: SoftServe makes second-order optimization practical for massive, ill-conditioned neural networks by eliminating costly matrix decompositions and ad hoc curvature fixes.

papers.title: Local Support Learning

summary.tldr: Local Support Learning (LSL) prevents catastrophic forgetting in large pre-trained models without using prior data by pairing weight adapters with Gaussian Mixture Model gating functions that restrict updates to local input activation distributions.
key_points: Models catastrophic forgetting as a geometric problem in the input space of individual weight matrices.
Pairs a standard trainable weight adapter with a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) gating function.
Uses the GMM's rapid likelihood decay away from current training data to keep the adapter closed on inputs from prior learning phases.
Successfully retains pre-trained and fine-tuned capabilities across multiple phases in LLMs up to 7B parameters without relying on past data.
summary.why_it_matters: LSL enables continual post-training of 7B-parameter LLMs while preserving past capabilities without the compute and storage overhead of retaining prior dataset copies.

papers.title: Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes

summary.tldr: Where-OPD uses on-policy self-distillation with synthetic scenes, providing MLLM teachers with textual spatial coordinates to train students without human annotations or external models.
key_points: Provides teachers with textual, spatially grounded guidance (object identities and coordinates) from procedurally generated synthetic scenes.
Students learn to reproduce the teacher's multi-region visual evidence integration using only the uncropped image and query.
Achieves a 3.23-point average performance gain on real-world perception benchmarks (CVBench, V*, ZoomBench, BLINK, HR-Bench, MME-RealWorld) despite synthetic-only post-training.
Demonstrates performance gains on visual perception tasks including counting, document, and chart understanding.
summary.why_it_matters: It proves that synthetic, spatially guided self-distillation enables scalable MLLM post-training that transfers effectively to real-world visual perception without relying on human annotations or larger teacher models.

security.title: Top AI coding agent security resources — October 2026

summary.tldr: Adversa AI's October 2026 security roundup highlights critical vulnerabilities in AI coding agents, including git config hijacks, sandbox escapes, swapped plugin pins, and a leak of 13,000 screenshots.
key_points: Git config hijack vulnerabilities were identified across seven AI coding agents.
Security flaws led to sandbox escapes and swapped plugin pins.
A data leak exposed 13,000 screenshots related to AI coding agent usage.
summary.why_it_matters: These vulnerabilities demonstrate that AI coding agents introduce severe infrastructure risks, including unauthorized code execution, plugin tampering, and data exposure.

security.title: SAGE: Similarity-Based Cleaning of Poisoned Training Data from Verified Examples

summary.tldr: SAGE defends against clean-label data poisoning by using a generic feature extractor and non-parametric, similarity-weighted predictions built from a small set of verified clean and poisoned examples.
key_points: Relies on a very small set of expert-verified clean and poisoned examples to prevent model overfitting.
Employs a generic feature extractor pre-trained on a separate dataset to process inputs.
Detects poisoned training data using a non-parametric, similarity-weighted prediction algorithm against the verified set.
Evaluated against seven clean-label poisoning attack methods on standard benchmarks.
Demonstrates that the class distribution of verified clean examples impacts defense performance more than the raw count of verified examples.
summary.why_it_matters: SAGE drastically reduces the labor and cost of data verification by requiring only a handful of verified examples to successfully clean poisoned training sets.

security.title: AuraForge: Scaling Security Supervision for Training Coding Agents

summary.tldr: AuraForge synthesizes and validates executable security tests to scale security supervision, constructing the multi-language AuraGym benchmark to train coding agents via attack-oriented task synthesis and safeguards against reward hacking.
key_points: AuraGym provides 679 executable feature-implementation tasks from 344 repositories across Python, JavaScript, and TypeScript, covering 177 CWE categories.
AuraForge generates ~3x more test cases than human-written security baselines while reducing false-positive test rates by 83.23%.

Training Qwen3.5-4B with AuraForge test cases achieved higher performance gains (19.7 FuncPass / 6.2 SecPass) across three languages compared to using human-written security tests (14.9 FuncPass / 4.4 SecPass).
summary.why_it_matters: It enables scalable, automated reinforcement learning supervision that teaches LLM coding agents to generate secure software without relying on scarce human-written security test suites.

security.title: Do Defenses Against LLM Extraction Work Across Attacks? A Lifecycle Benchmark of Black-Box Model Extraction

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced MEA-Bench, a unified, reproducible benchmark evaluating six black-box LLM extraction attacks, ten defenses, and two adaptive attacks under controlled model configurations, query budgets, and held-out evaluation conditions.
key_points: Evaluates 6 model extraction attacks, 10 defenses, and 2 adaptive attacks (paraphrasing and back-translation) under unified text-only API access conditions.
Measures surrogate model capability, fidelity to the victim LLM, output quality via Rep-4, and sensitivity to query budgets.
Evaluates adaptive attacks by jointly measuring provenance-detector scores alongside the fidelity and capability of surrogates trained on rewritten outputs.
Provides open-source code and artifacts via the MEA-Bench repository.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables standardized, fair comparisons of LLM extraction attacks and defenses by removing confounding variables like unequal query budgets and inconsistent evaluation metrics.

security.title: Sapien: A Stateful Policy Engine for Autonomous AI Agents

summary.tldr: Sapien is a stateful policy engine that enforces contextual security policies on AI agent tool calls using regular expressions extended with stateful predicates, deferred policy generation, and scoped semantic checks.
key_points: Sapien specifies permitted tool-call sequences by combining extended regular expressions, stateful predicates, deferred policy generation, and scoped semantic checks.
Maintains task performance within a few percent of an unconstrained AI agent's utility.
Rules out 93-95% of attacks on AgentDojo and 62-85% of attacks on Toolathlon when an agent is fully hijacked.
Blocks twice as many attacks as traditional tool allowlists on long-horizon tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: Sapien provides robust security for multi-step autonomous AI agents by restricting rogue actions based on execution history without significantly degrading task utility.

security.title: Backdoor Purification for LoRA-Tuned LLMs via Null-Space Projection

summary.tldr: A novel backdoor purification method for LoRA-tuned LLMs uses null-space projection to eliminate backdoor triggers without prior trigger knowledge, clean references, or post-hoc retraining.
key_points: Removes the need for strong traditional assumptions like trigger prior knowledge, clean reference datasets, or aggressive retraining.
Extracts backdoor directions via data curation and feature approximation to construct orthogonal null spaces for input and output channels per layer or head.
Projects LoRA updates onto the constructed null spaces without requiring post-hoc retraining of suspect parameters.
Reduces the attack success rate (ASR) from nearly 100% to under 10% in empirical evaluations.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows practitioners to securely deploy compromised LoRA adapters without sacrificing general model capabilities, downstream skills, or spending compute on retraining.

security.title: Backdoor Containment via Expert Quarantine and Shutdown in LLMs

summary.tldr: Researchers introduce Quarantined Expert Shutdown (QES), a defense that channels LLM backdoor triggers into a designated MoE-like expert during training, enabling complete backdoor mitigation at deployment by zeroing that expert's routing weight.
key_points: Presents a 'learn, but channel' strategy that allows backdoor formation during training but isolates trigger behavior into a dedicated, quarantined component.
Implements QES by augmenting Transformer models with routed expert-specific LoRA branches, lightweight routers, and auxiliary routing objectives.
Enables deployment-time mitigation via a single constant-time operation that zeros the quarantined expert's routing weight without requiring trigger screening or weight updates.
Reduces the attack success rate (ASR) from 100% to 0–10% across most tested settings spanning two tasks, three attacks, and four LLM families while maintaining utility.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a new paradigm for LLM security that neutralizes hidden backdoors at deployment with minimal computational overhead and without modifying core weights or screening inputs.

security.title: Towards Hierarchical Cyber Defense with Large Language Models: From Planning to Execution

summary.tldr: Researchers demonstrate that frozen, zero-shot LLMs can serve as scale-invariant cyber defense planners and executors, eliminating the need for network-specific reinforcement learning retraining.
key_points: Evaluated hierarchical defense using RL+RL, LLM+RL, and LLM+LLM configurations on small, medium, and large networks in the Cyberwheel environment.
Replacing only the strategic planner with an LLM yields limited gains as network size increases, emphasizing the necessity of strong tactical execution.
A frozen, general-purpose 70B LLM used for both planning and execution held attacker lateral movement to ~1% of steps and impact near zero across all network scales without task-specific retraining.
Evaluated six LLMs ranging from 3B to 70B parameters, including two cybersecurity-specialized models, against a MITRE ATT&CK-mapped automated red team.
summary.why_it_matters: Using capable frozen LLMs in a hierarchical defense architecture allows security systems to scale across different network sizes without time-consuming and costly RL retraining.

security.title: No One Architecture Fits All: A Cross-Environment Evaluation of Hierarchical Red Team Agents

summary.tldr: A controlled cross-environment evaluation reveals a performance inversion where RL+RL red team architectures excel in compact, densely rewarded networks, while LLM+LLM architectures dominate large, escalation-gated networks.
key_points: Evaluated RL+RL and LLM+LLM red team architectures against autonomous defenders across 18 configurations in CybORG CAGE-4 and two Cyberwheel network scales.
RL+RL outperformed LLM+LLM in CAGE-4 (78.5% vs. 18.0% disruption success) and the 100-host Cyberwheel network (81.0% vs. 50.5%).
LLM+LLM outperformed RL+RL in the 1010-host Cyberwheel network (55.0% vs. 0.0% disruption success).

Kill-chain analysis revealed distinct bottlenecks: RL+RL stalls at privilege escalation in large networks, whereas LLM agents obtain privileged access in CAGE-4 but fail to convert it into operational impact.
summary.why_it_matters: Red team architecture performance does not generalize across environments, meaning hybrid designs must be tailored to address specific, environment-dependent failure modes.

security.title: Homomorphic Advantage Operator: Stabilizing Reinforcement Learning Under Fully Homomorphic Encryption Constraints

summary.tldr: The Homomorphic Advantage Operator (HAO) stabilizes FHE-based reinforcement learning by applying a zero-mean centering projection to temporal-difference targets, preventing Bellman drift without adding multiplicative depth or ciphertext bootstrapping.
key_points: Eliminates Bellman drift by using a linear zero-mean centering projection that annihilates the uniform state-value baseline while preserving action rankings.

Achieved 0% polynomial approximation boundary breaches across all random seeds, compared to 83.8% episode breaches in the unstabilized baseline and breaches in 3 of 5 seeds using standard regularization.
Evaluated via tabular MDPs, an encrypted CartPole environment using CKKS, and a 20-node logistics routing benchmark with dense continuous features.
Improved optimal policy accuracy by 18.0 percentage points in tabular domains and demonstrated stability under DP-SGD-style Gaussian noise.
summary.why_it_matters: HAO enables stable, encrypted deep reinforcement learning on untrusted cloud infrastructure without relying on computationally expensive ciphertext bootstrapping operations.

security.title: Can AI Oversight Be Zero Knowledge?

summary.tldr: Researchers prove that zero-knowledge proofs and debate for general oracle-aided AI oversight are impossible in the random oracle model, but fully achievable if the oracle cryptographically signs its answers.
key_points: In the random oracle model, zero-knowledge proofs for general oracle-aided computations do not exist, even if prover and verifier run significantly longer than the computation itself.
This impossibility result extends to debate models used for scalable AI oversight.

By requiring the oracle to attach a cryptographic signature to its answers, every oracle-aided computation can be verified in zero knowledge with an efficient prover and verifier under collision-resistant hash function assumptions.
The signed-oracle approach enables scalable oversight without assuming an honest opponent in debate or computation robustness in single-prover protocols.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes the fundamental theoretical limits of private AI oversight and offers a practical cryptographic path to verify confidential model outputs without exposing underlying sensitive data.

summary.tldr: SafeDepth is a lightweight, plug-in framework that uses a router and adapter to dynamically select Transformer layer execution, reducing computation and harmful responses while keeping the backbone model frozen.
key_points: Existing token-level adaptive models show higher harmful-response rates than full-depth backbones, as safety features depend on layer execution, layer position, and inference phase (prompt vs. generation).
SafeDepth trains a lightweight router and adapter to bypass computations that lead to unsafe outputs while retaining those necessary for harmful request recognition and safe refusals.
The framework keeps the pretrained backbone frozen, avoiding additional pretraining.
Evaluated on Llama-3-8B-Instruct, SafeDepth dropped HarmBench-HJ unsafe responses from 55.44% to 25.25% compared to FlexiDepth.
SafeDepth reduced the XSTest false-refusal rate from 12.0% to 4.0% while maintaining performance on benign tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables token-level early exiting and layer skipping in LLMs to improve compute efficiency without suffering the safety degradation common in existing adaptive execution frameworks.

security.title: Identity-Bound Governance Under Execution Uncertainty: An Accountability Proof Block for LLM Agent Persistent Halts, with Cryptographic Implementation and Cross-Model Calibration

summary.tldr: This paper introduces the Accountability Proof Block (APB), a cryptographic mechanism using Ed25519 signatures and RFC 8785 canonicalization to resolve identity-bound governance halts in LLM agents where automated authority fails.
key_points: Formulates the Accountability Proof Block (APB) combining system-constructed evidence, human decision blocks, and Ed25519 cryptographic signatures bound to registered principals.
Proves four formal theorems: Protocol-Bounded Governance Completeness, Non-Repudiability, Impossibility of Anonymous Re-Authorization, and Finite-Time APB Construction Termination.
Achieved zero unresolved cases over 3,812 halt events, 100% detection of 1,800 attack attempts across 9 vectors, and 0 false acceptances in 2,000 multi-principal key-capture attempts.
Evaluated six open LLMs to show that drift threshold T* is intra-model stable (sigma/T* < 2%) but varies non-monotonically with model size, requiring per-deployment calibration.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a mathematically proven and empirically verified protocol for safely transferring authority to human operators when LLM agent observability fails.

security.title: A Hybrid Approach to Malware Detection: Integrating Few-Shot Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning with Autoencoders

summary.tldr: A new hybrid framework combines an Autoencoder Feature Extractor with Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning to enable robust malware detection using limited labeled data.
key_points: The Autoencoder Feature Extractor (AFE) compresses input data into low-dimensional latent features to remove noise.
The Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML) classifier enables rapid model adaptation to novel malware strains in few-shot settings.
Evaluated on the Ransomware Dataset 2024 across 1-shot to 50-shot binary classification tasks, maintaining high accuracy, F1 score, and Matthews Correlation Coefficient.
summary.why_it_matters: This architecture allows security systems to reliably detect novel ransomware strains even when extremely few labeled samples are available.

security.title: A Structured State Space Sequence Model for Multi-Class Classification of Malware

summary.tldr: This paper introduces the first empirical application of the Structured State Space Sequence (S4) model to multi-class malware detection and classification, outperforming traditional deep learning architectures by capturing long-range dependencies in malware execution flows.
key_points: Proposes an S4-based framework that discretizes malware sample sequences to capture long-range dependencies and map execution flows.
presents the first empirical application of Structured State Space Sequence models specifically for malware analysis.
Provides a comprehensive benchmark performance comparison between the S4 model and existing deep learning architectures for IoT malware classification.
summary.why_it_matters: Applying S4 models to malware sequence classification enables more effective detection of complex, long-range attack patterns to help secure rapidly expanding IoT ecosystems.

infra.title: Building a High-Performance and Portable vLLM Linear Backend with Helion

summary.tldr: Helion was integrated into vLLM's linear backend to replace manual GEMM implementations with an autotuned, high-level kernel DSL.
key_points: A single Helion GEMM implementation covers multiple algorithmic variants, including Standard GEMM, Split-K, and Swap-AB, via per-shape autotuning.

On NVIDIA Hopper GPUs, the Helion backend combined per-shape tuning with hybrid dispatch to outperform vLLM's default CUTLASS and DeepGEMM backends, achieving over 10% throughput improvement on some workloads.
Helion formulates kernel tuning as a structured numerical optimization problem over an ahead-of-time (AOT) search space, supplemented by LLM-guided search.
A primary challenge is the ahead-of-time tuning overhead, which can take hours due to fine-grained tuning strategies.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables LLM serving engines to automatically generate hardware-optimized, high-throughput linear kernels without requiring manual kernel specialization or expert engineering effort.

infra.title: Fine-tune a search agent with multi-turn RL on Amazon SageMaker AI

summary.tldr: Amazon SageMaker AI MTRL enables fine-tuning small LLM search agents using multi-turn reinforcement learning and policy gradient algorithms across complete interaction trajectories without needing expert SFT demonstrations.
key_points: MTRL optimizes agents across multi-step sequences using rewards based on the final outcome, bypassing the limitations of single-turn RL and SFT.
Provides serverless, asynchronous rollout and trajectory collection with bounded off-policy staleness to parallelize generation and gradient updates.
Includes a native algorithm library featuring PPO, CISPO, IS losses, and group-based advantage estimators like GRPO, GRPO pass@k, and RLOO.
Offers observability through managed MLflow to inspect turn-by-turn trajectories, custom reward functions, and tool loops.
summary.why_it_matters: Fine-tuning smaller models via multi-turn RL delivers the multi-step reliability of large frontier models at lower latency and inference costs.
